County Assessor
THE COUNTY ASSESSOR’S OFFICE IS CURRENTLY DOING THE REQUIRED SIX-YEAR COMMERCIAL REVIEW. State law requires commercial properties to be physically reviewed once every six (6) years. This review helps ensure fair and accurate property assessments for all Knox County property owners. Thank you for your cooperation that helps us maintain fair, accurate, and up-to-date property records for all Knox County taxpayers. We appreciate your time and assistance as we complete this state-required six-year commercial property review. If you have any questions, please contact the Knox County Assessor’s Office at 402-288-5601.
OUR APPRAISAL STAFF WILL: VISIT WITH THE PROPERTY OWNER – we may stop by to introduce ourselves and answer any questions you may have; REVIEW PROPERTY INFORMATION – we will review buildings, land, and other property information to ensure accuracy; IF ANY ISSUES WITH STRUCTURE – we will visit with you about any issues or concerns; TAKE NEW PHOTOS – we will take new photos of the exterior of the property; CARRY OFFICIAL IDENTIFICATION – our appraisal staff will carry official Knox County identification at all times.
Christa Beckmann
Assessor
402-288-5601
402-288-5602 – Fax
assessor@knoxcountyne.gov
County Assessor
Duties and Qualifications
The County Assessor is an elected official who has the general supervision over and the direction of the assessment of all property in his or her county. The duties are prescribed by Nebraska Statutes, Rules and Regulations (Chapter 77), which have the effect of law. The following is a partial list of those duties:
Administer the assessment statutes of Nebraska law.
Establish and maintain fair and equitable value on all real and personal property within the county.
Attend all meetings of the County Board of Equalization.
Review all applications for religious, charitable and educational tax exemptions.
Maintain cadastral records (i.e., parcel maps) on all property in the county.
Prepare abstract of value and certification of taxes levied for State Property Tax Administrator.
Prepare annual tax roll for the County Treasurer.
The County Assessor must hold and maintain a valid certificate.
Attend mandatory workshops.
Obtain a minimum of 30 hours of continued education bi-yearly.
